subject: literature
passage: For forty years, Anselm had rowed the ferry across the river below the mill, and he claimed he could read the water the way other men read a newspaper. His nephew Piet, who had taken over the crossing that spring, did not believe him. The river looked the same to Piet every morning: brown, slow, and ______ the old man would stand on the bank, watch a leaf drift past, and announce that the current had shifted toward the far shore overnight. By midsummer Piet had stopped arguing, because the old man was never wrong.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "The river looked the same to Piet every morning: brown, slow, and indifferent" is an independent clause, and "the old man would stand on the bank …" is another. The coordinating conjunction "yet" can join them, but it needs a comma before it and no punctuation after it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction such as "yet" need a comma before the conjunction; without it, "indifferent yet the old man" runs the clauses together.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A comma belongs before "yet," not after it; the second comma cuts the conjunction off from the clause it introduces.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A colon cannot be placed in front of a coordinating conjunction; it would separate "yet" from the clause it belongs to.
explanation.D: Correct. A comma followed by "yet" correctly joins the two independent clauses.
